Utilities

Functions for writing results to file, for reading results from said file, and for plotting results.

utils.match_to_grid(summary, mod_var_name, scan_type)[source]

Function to subset result data to contain only items that match some grid. This is needed for the boxplot that does not treat the x-axis as continuous.

utils.parse_results(mod_var_name='mu_X', file_name='./results/results.csv', field_names=['pri_Y_mean', 'post_Y_mean', 'potential_outcome_A1_mean', 'potential_outcome_A0_mean'])[source]

Reads result-file and extracts the requested fields to a numpy-array for e.g. easy plotting. By default, these are the expected Y-values given the agent’s prior and posterior beliefs, the true Y values with and without treatment, and the standard deviations for all of these.

Parameters:

  • mod_var_name (str) – Name of variable of interest (variable that was modified from defaults). Selects only corresponding rows from from the result-file.

  • file_name (str) – Path and file name of result-file.

  • field_names ([str]) – List of strings containing the column names of interest to extract from the result-file.

utils.plot_CATE_for_var(var, mean_of_x, std_of_x, x_label, file_name, x_lim, y_lim, scan)[source]
Parameters:

  • var (str) – Name of variable of interest

  • mean_of_x (float) – Mean of horizontal scale (x) to center on.

  • std_of_x (float) – Standard deviation of the horizontal scale (x). Used for normalizing plot.

  • x_label (str) – Label that will be visible under the x-axis

  • file_name (str) – File name and path of the result file to parse.

  • x_lim ((float, float)) – +-Limits of horizontal axis

  • y_lim ((float, float)) – +-Limits of vertical axis

Notes: Uncertainty of true model (with default values) is tiny.

file_name (str) – Path and name of result file.

utils.plot_all(file_name='./results/results_18_2.csv')[source]

Function that reads in all results from ./results/results.csv and creates boxplots for all variables found in column “Modified variables”. Note that the plotting methods are custom made for specific plots and might need tweaking with new data (e.g. plot ranges).

utils.read_outcomes_from_file(file_name='./results/results.csv')[source]

This function reads in results from the results.csv file. The function extracts the outcome under the true SCM given the agent’s decision based on their posterior beliefs, and separates this by name of modified prior and groups the results by unique values of the modified prior.

E.g. results_summary[‘N_E_mu’][‘parameter_values’] contains a list of unique values that N_E_mu have taken in the results.csv-file, and results_summary[‘N_E_mu’][‘value_lists’] contains lists of outcomes where every list corresponds to the parameter value at corresponding index and every item in the list is the outcome for one randomly sample X_o.

Parameters:

file_name (str) – Path and file name of results file.

  • path (str) – Path where to store result file.
